industry.ev: Bosch's own prognosis (May-2026): the overall Indian vehicle market grows 3-4% a year to 2033, with battery-electric penetration rising in buses, small (<2t) LCVs and cars on total cost of ownership. Power Solutions (fuel injection, engine management) is ICE content; RBIC's braking and safety content is powertrain-agnostic (EVs need new braking systems such as iBooster for regeneration). Bosch's e-axle entry is through a 50:50 JV with Tata AutoComp (first shipments Q3 of calendar 2027).

moat: Parent technology and IP
Strong
Access to Robert Bosch GmbH's products and R&D (~87k researchers group-wide); first to bring ESP/ABS to India (RBIC); 'best in technology' OEM awards (Q1FY27)
The reason OEMs buy Bosch; but it is rented, not owned: royalty and technical fees were Rs478 cr (2.4% of revenue, +29%) in FY26
Position in engine management and fuel injection
Strong (ICE)
Power Solutions grew 17.6% in FY26 and 29% in Q1FY27, ahead of production; 2-wheeler EMS share gains ('we've gained market share', Aug-2026). Market shares not disclosed
High share in a technology that shrinks as EVs grow; regulation (CAFE 3, OBD) keeps adding content for now
Safety and braking (RBIC)
Strong
'Dominant market presence' in ESP/ABS, airbag ECUs and sensors; 17% revenue CAGR FY23-25; EBITDA margin 12.8% to 19.3%; order book 'very, very full'
Powertrain-agnostic and regulation-driven: the best part of the business, now owned
Aftermarket brand and reach
Moderate
Bosch brand, workshop programme, lubricants, batteries, filters; growth only 3.7% in FY26, 9.6% in Q1FY27 after 'corrections in strategy'
A cash cow that had stalled; the recovery is one quarter old
Cost position
Weak-Moderate
58% of purchases from related parties; purchases of traded goods Rs7,987 cr (40% of revenue); gross margin -420bp YoY in Q1FY27; EBITDA margin 12-14% vs Schaeffler, Sona and ZF CV at 16-24%
A large part of the value chain sits with the parent: margins are structurally lower than the brand suggests
Electrification
Weak / unproven
E-axles via a 50:50 JV (Tata AutoComp, first shipments 2027); EV revenue 'not showing up in terms of turnover' (MD, Aug-2026)
Bosch shares the economics of its EV entry; the ICE franchise has no like-for-like replacement yet
critiques: A 40-plus P/E is rich for mid-teen EPS growth, even with RBIC.
Fairly valued at 44.6x/41.4x FY27E/FY28E after a strong quarter.
RBIC was bought cheaply (10.6x EV/EBITDA) relative to Bosch's own ~40x: good for minorities.
Powertrain and ICE exposure remains the long-term risk.

Related-party flows are large and rising: royalty plus group professional fees Rs1,575 cr (7.9% of revenue) in FY26 vs Rs1,255 cr in FY25; 58% of purchases are from the group; Rs950 cr lent to group companies.
Earnings history is flattered by business sales to the group and others (Rs785 cr gain in FY24, Rs556 cr in FY26): reported EPS overstates the run-rate by 15-35% in those years.

conflicts: Q1FY27 consolidated PAT: Rs704.9 cr (Free Press Journal/PTI), Rs705 cr (Upstox body; headline Rs795 cr) and Rs706.1 cr with EPS Rs239.41 (Kotak Neo). We use Rs706.1 cr, which matches the EPS.

Screener's Sep-2025 and Jun-2026 quarters show RBIC-restated figures from the Nov-2026 filing (e.g. Q1FY27 revenue Rs7,167 cr); the numbers reported at the time were Rs4,795 cr and Rs5,842 cr. We use the as-reported numbers (BOSCHLTD.patch.js).
A search summary attributed the Rs54,050 target to UBS with an 'accumulate' rating; UBS's last target we can verify is Rs45,530 (Buy, 12-Jun-2026). We list the Rs54,050 target as unnamed.
Exports: management said ~8-8.5% of revenue (Aug-2026); the FY26 directors' report shows export sales of Rs1,492 cr (7.4%) and overseas revenue of Rs1,629 cr (8.1%).
MOSL's FY27E balance sheet (11-Aug-2026) keeps investments rising to Rs11,095 cr, which does not appear to deduct the ~Rs9,060 cr RBIC payment; our forecast does.
